subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm designing a compact but detailed static model: a six-wheeled armoured hauler truck with a cab, flatbed cargo pod, turret, and neon glow accents, since it can skip joints entirely as a static build, and I'm working out rough dimensions for the body.

Planning the wheel axle positions, cab and hood geometry, and texture placements for hazard stripes, headlights, windshield, and cyber-rune details using box and cylinder primitives and a glow kit import.

Still computing windshield plane placement...

Now I'm adding side windows, front bumper with hazard texture, headlight glow boxes, and a magenta roof light bar to round out the cab's details.

Next I'm shaping the roof turret with its cylinder base and barrel rods, then building the flatbed deck and a hex-prism cargo pod with banded glow strips and biohazard decal plating.

I realize 8-sided cylinders put vertices at the sides rather than flat faces there, so I'm switching to 10 sides, calculating the apothem to size the decal face properly, but noticing the resulting face width is quite narrow for the decal I wanted to place.

Actually, I'm abandoning the cylinder approach entirely in favor of building the pod from chamfered boxes: a main rectangular body with smaller boxes rotated 45° at the corners to create beveled edges, which gives a cleaner low-poly look with flat sides for decals.

Actually, let me skip the chamfer approach and extrude an octagon cross-section along the z-axis for the pod body, giving it a rounded, chamfered-corner shape instead of a plain box. I'm defining the octagon profile with half-width and half-height plus a 0.4 chamfer, then placing side decals on the flat faces.

Thinking about text orientation for readability, I'll avoid putting labels on the curved sides and instead reserve a short label like "SEALED" for the rear door where orientation is simpler to get right, while keeping the side panels mostly icon-based to dodge mirrored-text issues. Then I'll add banded ribs along the pod's length using rows of boxes with glowing strips for detail.

Now I'm placing the seal details and guard elements: a glowing lock strip along the pod's top, rear gun sponsons, side rails, a rear light bar, exhaust stacks behind the cab, side fuel tanks, an antenna, a searchlight, and a roof-mounted turret on the cab with a cylindrical base and boxy head.

Adding twin barrel rods and glowing muzzle tips...

I'm also planning underglow neon strips beneath the chassis sides in cyan, and defining the overall color palette of dark gunmetal hull with magenta, cyan, and yellow hazard accents, along with a procedural paint function that varies shading by surface normal, adds seam lines along the side panels, and darkens the lower hull with grime using noise-based blending.

Now I'm sketching out texture details: hazard stripe patterns for bumpers and skirts, a license plate and windshield texture, a hexagonal shield emblem in cyan, and a cyberpunk-style text label reading "HAUL-07" instead of risky custom glyphs. I'm also defining wheel geometry with dark tire cylinders, metal hub cylinders, and a thin glowing cyan ring at the hub face.

Working out fenders as dark boxes positioned over each wheel, checking that chassis height and wheel placement keep everything grounded properly, and sizing the overall vehicle width to feel like a proper armoured hauler with dual rear axles and a cargo pod spanning most of the rear deck.

I'm also planning the helper functions: a basic box builder for parts with mirrored placement, confirming static parts don't need joints, and a decal/plane helper for applying textures like markings onto flat surfaces.

I'm sketching out the texture designs needed: a hazard stripe pattern, a tinted windshield with HUD-style reflections, a hex-shield emblem in magenta and cyan, a rear plate, and a side sign reading "HAUL-07" with decorative kanji.

I still need to add grille slats, warning strip lights, a cargo pod with rear doors and an emblem, lock bars, a sensor antenna near the cab, and possibly side turrets or missile pods on the pod corners. I'm also checking that the wheels, bumper, skirts, and underglow all sit correctly above the ground plane without clipping.

I'm now adding rivet details along the pod ribs and cab sides using small repeated boxes, then recalculating the cab's position and windshield slope geometry so the roof height and glass angle line up properly with the chassis.

Next I'm placing the hood front, headlights, and grille texture plane with widths balanced so the grille and lights fit symmetrically on the hood, then working out the side window cutout region on the cab profile.

Now I'm positioning the roof light bar with a magenta/cyan glow split down the middle, setting the turret location on the roof so its barrels extend forward past the hood without clipping, and placing exhaust stacks behind the cab.

Next I'm working out the deck geometry sitting on the chassis top, placing the octagonal pod so its bottom edge aligns flush with the deck surface, then adding cradle clamp boxes on either side of the deck.

Adding ribs with glow stripes...

Right side mirrors the same logic for s=-1. Now I'm placing the rear door texture on the pod's octagon face, sizing the emblem to fit within the cut corners, then positioning the front sensor module, rear bumper with hazard plate and tail light glow boxes, and side skirt panels between the wheel wells.

Checking skirt placement against axle positions to make sure it spans the gap between front and middle wheels without clipping, settling on a skirt at z=0.8 with a hazard decal, then noting I'll skip fuel tanks/batteries for now and just add a simple battery cell detail.

Adding glowing cyan window boxes on the skirt and a rear antenna with a glowing tip for the cab. For the hull paint logic, I'm mixing a lighter top color with darker panel seam lines, grime near the base, and noise-based scratches for wear, applying this only to cab/hood/hull parts while keeping other components flat-colored and giving the pod its own distinct paint treatment.

Now I'm defining the pod's paint as an off-white steel tone with cyan trim accents and stenciled wear patterns, using position-based seams in model space. Time to write the full implementation, aiming for roughly 350 lines.
